title: Year-end Reflection, Team Pulse, and Squad Rotations
summary: Leadership walked through the year highlights, product milestones, a modest hiring slow-down, and a set of squad rotations to balance capacity for Redwood Dedicated and Private. People Ops covered comp cycle dates and support for teammates. Session ended with open Q&A and concrete follow-ups.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Start time: 09:00 PST / 17:00 UTC
Duration: ~78 minutes
Attendees: Elena Park (CEO), Marco Ruiz (CTO), Jin Park (Head of Eng), Priya Desai (Head of Product), Sam Ortiz (Head of People), Maya Liu (Comms), + ~140 employees
Recording (internal): https://replay.internal/redwood/allhands/2026-12-08 (note: internal only)

Auto-generated summary (may be rough):
Leadership reviewed topline growth and infra investments, announced small hiring slow-down but no layoffs, described squad rotations to mitigate Dedicated capacity risk, and recapped people timeline for comp/bonus. Open Q&A covered remote policy, support for new on-call, and benchmarking asks.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Elena: Hey folks, thanks for joining, um, we're gonna jump in. Quick admin — recording is on, transcript as usual. Big thanks to everyone for, uh, shipping the quantization work in Q4, huge effort, thank you.
[00:28] Marco: Quick note on infra, just to set context — we've pushed the new kernel selector into prod on a small percent of traffic, latency looks stable, cost reduction is showing but there are, ah, a few tail cases we need to look at.
[00:49] Jin: Yeah, we saw the rarer OOM on p4x instances when sequence lengths spiked, so we're refining the KV cache eviction policy — it's, uh, partly why we want to shuffle some capacity around.
[01:12] Priya: On product side, roadmap deck is in the drive, link in chat, I'm going to share a marked-up version after this with squad-level notes. We need squads to align on what 'Dedicated-first' features are highest priority.
[01:40] Audience (someone): Quick question — are we doing layoffs?
[01:45] Elena: No, not at all. We're, um, pausing open requisitions in some non-critical areas to conserve runway, but no reductions in force. We want to be clear about that.
[02:10] Sam: And to add, People Ops is scheduling 1:1 office hours for anyone with questions about pay, comp, and support. We'll post FAQ later today.
[02:36] Marco: Back to infra — we might route a small percentage of Dedicated traffic to the older quant path as a fallback during peak to avoid SLO breaches. This is about graceful degradation, not sacrificing customers.
[02:58] Elena: Good, and remember our thesis — serving matters. We have to balance cost and latency, and sometimes that means routing policy tweaks.
[03:20] [slide change] Priya: Ok, visualizing the squad rotations — we're moving three engineers from Model Onboarding to Dedicated performance squad for Q1, and two PMs will be temporarily reallocated to Support Ops to accelerate post-deploy metrics.
[03:46] Jin: Logistical note — on-call handovers should be documented. If you're moving squads please create at least one runbook entry and pair for a week.
[04:05] Audience (someone else): What's the criteria for choosing who rotates?
[04:12] Priya: We prioritized cross-trained folks and volunteers first, then balanced by seniority so we don't create gaps. If you're concerned, talk to your manager — we tried to be transparent.
[04:40] [audible chuckle]
[04:45] Marco: Competitor note — LargeCloud AI announced a managed offering that looks similar to our Dedicated pitch, but it's, uh, less configurable at the network level; it's an opportunity for differentiation.
[05:08] Elena: And we've seen modelX open-sourced some stuff, but our position is production reliability + observability. Keep that in customer-facing story.
[05:30] Maya: Posting the annotated slides: internal link (deck): internal://allhands/yrend-2026-deck — will attach transcript and the pulse survey.
[05:52] [short tech demo clip played by Marco - audio overlapping]
[06:20] Marco: Demo notes — auto-batching improvements reduce peak token cost by ~12% on median workloads; however, some long-seq gen still poorly amortizes, that's on the backlog.
[06:45] Jin: We'll run micro-benchmarks focusing on the worst 5% tail cases — expected to deliver runbook + perf numbers in two weeks.
[07:08] Audience: How will this affect availability for Private customers with air-gapped set-ups?
[07:16] Marco: For Private we keep a stricter isolation path, but some optimizations are only doable in hosted infra. We'll document which improvements are available where. There may be tradeoffs in time-to-rollout.
[07:44] Priya: People Ops update — comp and bonus timelines: calibrations finish by Dec 14, managers will receive letters Dec 16-17, payouts in Jan payroll. If you have equity questions we'll have a session next week.
[08:12] Sam: We're also extending an assistance program for folks relocating over the next quarter — people managers will receive the policy docs.
[08:34] Audience: Any change to remote-first policy next year?
[08:40] Elena: No policy shift planned — we are keeping remote-first, but we'll pilot regional meetups in Q2 2027 for cross-team collaboration.
[09:05] [pause, typing noises]
[09:18] Priya: Quick follow-up on squad rotations — managers, please post a short note on OKR impacts and dependency owners by Friday.
[09:35] Jin: Also, we are adjusting the on-call credit policy slightly for rotated engineers to account for the extra cognitive load — details in the runbook.
[09:55] Audience: Will this slow down feature work?
[10:01] Elena: Short-term reprioritization yes, but it's intentional to stabilize product quality and lower unit costs. We expect to reallocate capacity back into feature work mid-Q1.
[10:24] [Q&A segment begins]
[10:31] Audience (Ana, Eng): I volunteered for rotation and wonder about career tracks — will this count as promotion experience?
[10:40] Sam: Absolutely, rotational work is legit growth. Managers will capture impact narratives for performance cycles.
[10:55] Audience (Sales): Are we changing pricing because of Dedicated cost wins?
[11:03] Priya: Not immediately. We'll model price implications for next year's plan; for now any price change needs exec signoff.
[11:28] Audience (Support): Heard mention of fallback routing — does that mean customers might see model differences?
[11:35] Marco: In rare cases yes, fallbacks might hit slightly smaller model variants. We will flag this in logs and allow customers to opt into strict consistency.
[11:55] Audience (someone): Pulse question — will hiring reopen in Q2?
[12:02] Elena: We aim to recalibrate in Q2 2027; decisions depend on macro and performance against our cost-savings targets.
[12:20] [audible "uh" and shuffling]
[12:30] Priya: Product spotlight — we shipped better structured output hooks for tool-calling; adoption is at 18% on the new flows. Shoutout to the infra and SDK team.
[12:52] Jin: Thanks team. Ops note: If your service is impacted by the kernel change, file a support ticket with tag "kernel-22" so we can prioritize.
[13:12] [laughter]
[13:18] Maya: Pulse survey link in chat — please give candid feedback about rotations and support. It's anonymous.
[13:30] Elena: Closing — grateful for the year, the engineering wins, and the discipline around costs. We'll get the decks and the survey out, and please use the office hours if you have concerns.
[13:50] [meeting ends; some side conversations continue as recording stops]

Notes about transcript: speaker labels may be rough and some proper nouns transcribed imperfectly (e.g., quantization shorthand, internal kernel names). Several times the transcript picked up cross-talk. For any crucial policy detail refer to the recording or posted deck.
